# Model building

Use the authenticated Biosimulant MCP for account work; preserve exact scoped approvals and ownership.

Keep lab.yaml authoritative, with local models described by model.yaml and the actual Python entrypoint. Use the requested algorithm and real input files. Inspect existing sources and preserve package identity and public interfaces. MRS/MTS are optional requested documents, not automatic prerequisites.

Use immutable workspace preview/apply operations for edits. Preserve base revision/diff/digest and authenticated approval. Pin dependencies and source artifacts when used. models/wiring form the executable graph; generic components/connections metadata does not.

Choose ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_BEFORE_RUN, EACH_WINDOW or ONCE_AFTER_RUN for real behavior. Implement BioModule.execute(inputs, *, context), returning typed outputs. Legacy advance_window modules remain supported. Keep model.yaml biosim.execution_policy consistent when declared. Tests should be collectable and executable with a compatible installed interpreter. Compile/import success is not a substitute for exercising requested software behavior. Test meaningful behavior; stateful snapshot/restore must preserve computation state.

Make a running model visibly alive. Print short progress lines with print(..., flush=True) after loading inputs, at each major phase (setup, solve, fit, export), about every 10% or 30 seconds inside long loops, and at the end. Include counts, units and elapsed time. Stay near 200 lines per run (runs keep the last 2,000) and never print full arrays or secrets. Stream wrapped child program output instead of buffering it. Logs supplement typed outputs; the result still goes on an output port.

Write files inside the execution working directory, expose typed file outputs and retain them after temporary directories close. VisualSpecs are useful when they answer the question, not mandatory. Preserve results when optional rendering fails.

Honor the current session execution policy, cumulative budget, ownership and exact scoped approvals. Inspect live tool schemas. Resume existing Labs, sessions and runs before creating new ones. Keep immutable revision IDs, checksums, original inputs and attribution. Never invent input data, measured values, files or successful execution. Do not rerun saved work just to inspect it.

Biosimulant has no scientific qualification or acceptance gate. Do not require MRS/MTS, evidence, caveats, independent fixtures, domain profiles or a research-ready target for ordinary analysis, execution or publication. Do not append generic biological-validity disclaimers. Run scientific reviews, reference comparisons or benchmarks only as requested work and return their findings as data. Explicit user conditions and ordinary permissions still apply.

Technical checks remain: readable manifests, safe paths and packaging, entrypoints, dependencies, types, shapes, formats, declared units and checksums. Preserve real solver/parser/subprocess errors and useful partial outputs. File-only tasks need no chart. With runtime 0.0.38+, use `ExecutionOutcome` and `report_execution_outcome` to record an inner command failure; do not mistake a saved error report for a completed analysis.

Read [Naming and identity](naming.md) before creating or renaming work. Preserve existing titles, package identities and aliases.
